Text: Your expedition teams return from a planet in the {HellPlanet} System

Furnace-hot and pressurised, the planet is deeply inhospitable. They braved this hellish world to investigate a buried structure. Now they confirm: it’s vast, metallic, and ancient.

{D(Techy)} cannot wait to dig it out.

{D(Techy)} can’t keep the wonder from {his(Techy)} voice. “Too unwieldy for battle; absurdly slow. It was a science ship - there are banks of ruined servers everywhere - but there’s an entire industrial plant, too. What were they making?”

In any case, the surviving servers are a boon to your scientists.

The science ark was a terraforming ship?

According to its logs, the so-called "Eden ship" was a project of the pre-Collapse League of Spacefaring Nations run by Galileo Institute scientists. It was designed to pump gases into a planet’s atmosphere, change its climate, and eventually seed life.

In the final entries, the crew - stranded after the Collapse - tried to terraform a planet in {HellPlanet}. Whether due to human error or insufficient resources, they created a “runaway greenhouse effect”, transforming the planet into a boiling hell-world.

But you wonder: if properly harnessed, could this ship's purpose be fulfilled? That could change everything.

That night, you dream of a forest on old Earth

The scent of pines. The gentle sun. Green leaves sighing in the breeze.

You awake to the hum of the station. A sterile cage of metal and plasteel. You stare out the window, breathing recycled air hundreds of years old, feeling the crushing weight of centuries of life in space.

Could that dream of a green world come to pass? It would be difficult - perhaps impossible.
Station living is a prison; the human race needs green fields!
